zh.title: 臺灣棒球隊搭乘星宇航空AIRSORAYAMA GOLD藝術機赴日
zh.summary: 臺灣棒球隊搭乘星宇航空JX800赴日，AIRSORAYAMA GOLD藝術機執飛。
body: 臺灣代表隊球員及教練今天上午搭乘星宇航空JX800班機赴日，星宇航空特別安排AIRSORAYAMA GOLD藝術機執飛。中職會長蔡其昌親自送機。2026年亞洲職棒冠軍爭霸賽預計12日起在日本東京巨蛋開打。
星宇航空表示，已準備「Fly In Gold! Go For Gold!」應援毛巾與茶包，致贈代表隊及當班旅客；也安排曾代表臺灣隊出賽的棒球女國手、現任空服組員張甄芸，在機艙門口與球員擊拳加油。

en.title: Taiwan Baseball Team Flies to Japan on STARLUX's AIRSORAYAMA GOLD Aircraft
en.summary: Taiwan's baseball team flew to Japan on STARLUX JX800 aboard an AIRSORAYAMA GOLD aircraft.
body: Taiwan's baseball team flew to Japan this morning on STARLUX Airlines flight JX800. STARLUX assigned an AIRSORAYAMA GOLD art aircraft to operate the flight. The professional baseball league's president also saw the team off. The 2026 Asian Professional Baseball Championship is expected to begin at Tokyo Dome in Japan on the 12th.

STARLUX said it prepared “Fly In Gold! Go For Gold!” cheering towels and tea bags for the team and passengers on the flight. The airline also arranged for a woman who had represented Taiwan in baseball and now works as a cabin-crew member to greet the players with fist bumps at the cabin door.

zh.title: 航空短訊彙整：波音將裁減商用飛機部門約5%職位 產量爬升慢於預期；菲律賓航空首開馬尼拉—芝加哥直飛：西向回程近17小時，每週3班A350執飛
zh.summary: 本期收錄2則獨立消息：波音將裁減商用飛機部門約5%職位 產量爬升慢於預期、菲律賓航空首開馬尼拉—芝加哥直飛：西向回程近17小時，每週3班A350執飛。
body: 本期彙整2則航空短訊，各則為獨立事件。部分內容摘自近期站內報導，原文與來源見文末。

1. 波音將裁減商用飛機部門約5%職位 產量爬升慢於預期
波音將裁減商用飛機部門約5%職位，受影響員工可能最早於12月收到通知。

2. 菲律賓航空首開馬尼拉—芝加哥直飛：西向回程近17小時，每週3班A350執飛
菲律賓航空11月9日首開馬尼拉—芝加哥直飛航線，每週3班、由A350-900執飛；西向回程表定16小時40分，是該公司迄今最長的美國航線，美國航點增至8個。

en.title: Aviation briefs: Boeing to Cut About 5% of Commercial Airplane Workforce as Output Slows; Philippine Airlines launches first nonstop Manila–Chicago service: near-17-hour westbound leg, three weekly A350 flights
en.summary: 2 independent updates: Boeing to Cut About 5% of Commercial Airplane Workforce as Output Slows; Philippine Airlines launches first nonstop Manila–Chicago service: near-17-hour westbound leg, three weekly A350 flights.
body: 2 independent aviation updates. Includes excerpts of recent reports, with original reports and sources linked below.

1. Boeing to Cut About 5% of Commercial Airplane Workforce as Output Slows
Boeing will cut about 5% of its commercial-airplane workforce; laid-off employees could receive notices as early as December.

2. Philippine Airlines launches first nonstop Manila–Chicago service: near-17-hour westbound leg, three weekly A350 flights
Philippine Airlines launches its first nonstop Manila–Chicago passenger service on November 9, operating three times a week with the Airbus A350-900; the westbound return is scheduled at 16 hours 40 minutes, making it the carrier's longest US route and lifting its US network to eight cities.

facts.claim: Boeing will cut about 5% of the jobs in its commercial airplane workforce as it builds jets more slowly than anticipated.
facts.sourceQuote: Boeing will cut about 5% of the jobs in its commercial airplane workforce as it builds jets more slowly than it had anticipated

facts.claim: The reduction would amount to about 2,500 jobs, based on the division's 50,500 employees at the end of 2025.
facts.sourceQuote: The reduction would amount to about 2,500 jobs based on the 50,500 people the division employed at the end of 2025.

facts.claim: Employees who will be laid off could receive notices as early as December, according to Pope's memo.
facts.sourceQuote: Employees who will be laid off could receive notices as early as December, according to Pope’s memo.

facts.claim: Pope wrote that adjusting production schedules and reducing aircraft output puts the operation in an overstaffed position.
facts.sourceQuote: “Adjusting our production schedules and reducing aircraft output puts us in an overstaffed position,” Pope wrote.

facts.claim: On its October earnings call, Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg said Boeing would miss its 737 delivery goal for 2026.
facts.sourceQuote: On its October earnings call, Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg pushed that target to early 2027 and said Boeing would miss its 737 delivery goal for 2026.

facts.claim: The 787 program was working toward 10 Dreamliners per month, but production held at eight per month in the third quarter.
facts.sourceQuote: The 787 program is also running behind. The company had been working toward 10 Dreamliners a month, but production held at eight a month in the third quarter.
